[E71] (bear) Screen reason (bear side): earnings growth decelerating | source: scanX signal engine This evidence suggests that Adani Enterprises' earnings growth rate is slowing down, which could imply a lack of sustainable momentum in its core business. A deceleration in earnings growth can be concerning and may indicate underlying problems such as rising costs or declining margins. [E66] (bull) Screen reason (bull side): Sales +1% YoY | source: scanX signal engine This evidence appears to contradict the other negative indicators, suggesting that Adani Enterprises' sales have grown by 1% year-over-year. However, this growth rate is extremely low and may not be sustainable in a competitive market environment. [E77] (bull) Sector median sales growth is 22.1%. | value: 22.1% | source: scanX sector tailwind This evidence provides context by showing that the company's sales growth of -27% over three years and -7% in the most recent period are significantly lower than the sector median of 22.1%. This disparity further supports the argument that Adani Enterprises is underperforming relative to its peers. Conceded: [E40] (neutral) CWIP stands at Rs 1083 Cr (Mar 2026), a +83.2% move on the prior year. CWIP up 83.2% (2025->2026): capex build-up phase — growth spend underway, watch for completion | value: 83.2% | source: the data provider - Mar 2026 This evidence suggests that Adani Enterprises is investing heavily in capital expenditures, which could be a positive sign of future growth potential. However, the high level of investment and the significant increase in CWIP (Capital Work-in-Progress) over one year may indicate a need for caution regarding the sustainability of these investments and their impact on current earnings. In conclusion, Adani Enterprises Ltd appears to be trading at an elevated valuation relative to its peers, with negative indicators such as declining sales growth
